title: Expose multi-customer expense allocation evidence in container workflows
description: Extend existing container loading and settlement workflows with read-only expense-allocation evidence from the canonical ERP-042 batches. Reuse the existing multi-customer and allocation models rather than creating another allocation engine. Do not post finance entries, rewrite settlement values, infer customer shares, execute production SQL, deploy, or release.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation audits and reuses ERP-042 canonical allocation batches and any existing container-customer relationship, leaving one authoritative persisted allocation model.
Container loading detail exposes active allocation-batch count, allocated amount by customer and currency, allocation basis and unallocated or unavailable context using only explicit persisted rows.
Existing container settlement workflows expose the same allocation evidence in separately labeled read-only fields and do not copy or write the values into authoritative settlement totals.
Different currencies are grouped separately and are never combined or converted without an authoritative persisted conversion already belonging to the source evidence.

Voided or superseded allocation rows are excluded from active totals but remain inspectable through explicit history; invalid customer or container links are shown as invalid or unavailable and are not reassigned.
Missing allocation evidence is shown as none or unknown and is never interpreted as zero expense, settled expense, receivable, payable or a legal customer statement.
The UI and documentation state that allocation rows are operational cost-distribution evidence, not accounting posting, payment authorization, tax treatment or settlement confirmation.
The workflow does not change container records, allocation batches, settlement documents, expenses, invoices, customer balances, inventory, tax or finance records.
Queries are bounded or paged, avoid per-row database access and keep legacy containers without allocation batches readable without request-time or production backfill.

Unit/integration tests cover one and multiple customers, multiple currencies, partial and missing allocations, void history, invalid historical links, bounded queries and source-record non-mutation; safe validation passes and browser acceptance is recorded as deferred during development.

scenarios: Open a multi-customer container with a partial ERP-042 allocation batch and verify customer, currency, basis and unallocated evidence in both loading and settlement views without changing settlement totals.
Inspect a container with voided, invalid or missing allocation evidence and verify it is not presented as settled, payable, receivable or posted and that no source record changes.

human_gate.reason: Read-only presentation of existing repository allocation evidence. Accounting posting, real settlement, production database mutation, deployment and release remain behind mandatory human gates.
